messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty P-9876 triggered -> high 5xx rate on inference-service-prod (svc: inference-v2). Paging sylvia (primary) and rajesh (secondary). Links: https://pd.redwood/p/P-9876 :rotating_light:

sylvia: saw the pager, jumping in. I’m on metro, ETA ~5m to keyboard. any customer-facing errors or just internal spikes?

mike: dashboards show 5xx spiking from ~00:42 UTC across all hosts in inference-v2. error type: KV_CACHE_MISS + downstream NRT timeout. RTTs also up ~150ms. Not widespread client errors yet but traffic pattern looks bursty (batch replay).

sylvia: thanks. rajesh are you able to take secondary? I’ll own triage and on-call comms.

rajesh: I’m available. taking secondary. if sylvia needs to hand off later I can continue.

lia: FYI customers using Dedicated pools in eu-west-1 saw increased tail latency 00:45-00:50 UTC, filed a quick note to account-sre. Might want to set temporary SLO adjustment so we don't page on noisy thresholds while we mitigate.

sylvia: agree. short plan: 1) mute noisy 5xx alert rule for 30m 2) adjust inference-latency-slo alert upper bound from 500ms -> 800ms for 1h as a temporary ramp 3) follow KV cache runbook to identify eviction storm and restart affected workers if needed.

mike: runbook pointer: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/kv-cache-eviction. key steps: check redis memory metrics, eviction events, and per-host cache hit rate.

sylvia: executing step 1 now. command to mute alert rule:
```bash
# on-call script to mute noisy alert
redwood-alert-cli mute --rule inference-5xx-rate --duration 30m --reason "kv-cache eviction storm, temp suppression"
```

incident-bot: Alert rule inference-5xx-rate muted by sylvia for 30m.

rajesh: I’ll start checking the cache metrics and host OOM logs. if we see consistent evictions we should consider rolling a small number of workers to clear local caches rather than global restart.

mike: seeing eviction_count spike on shard-3 and shard-7. Redis memory nearing 98% on those nodes. eviction policy is allkeys-lru. suspect an upstream spike of cold prefixes.

sylvia: ok. change 2 (adjust SLO thresholds) -- I’m proposing this JSON patch to our alerting config, applying as a temporary override via the web UI.

```json
{
  "alert": "inference-latency-p95",
  "old_threshold_ms": 500,
  "temp_threshold_ms": 800,
  "duration": "1h",
  "reason": "kv-cache eviction causing transient tail latency"
}
```

mike: approved. apply and annotate the change in the incident timeline.

sylvia: applied override and annotated: "temp SLO up to 800ms for 1h while investigating KV cache evictions". incident-bot shows config change event ID cfg-3321.

incident-bot: Config change recorded: cfg-3321 by sylvia.

rajesh: mitigation update: restarted worker group inference-worker-3 on shard-3 using canary restart script to avoid warmup stampede. cache-hit rates improved from 28% -> 68% within 90s.

lia: customer impact: no escalations filed yet, but a small set of real-time inference customers saw 2-3x latency. Noting outreach readiness if accounts ask.

sylvia: good. keep temp suppression in place. if error rate stays <15% of peak for next 15m we’ll lift worker restarts and start rolling a config bump to increase redis memory limit.

mike: creating remediation ticket: RD-5432 adjust redis maxmemory to reduce evictions. linking to post-incident action items.

rajesh: handoff note for next shift (cc @oncall-rotation): Primary: sylvia (handled mitigation) -> handing to rajesh at 02:15 UTC for monitoring and follow-ups. Secondary: mike. Coverage gap: none but be aware of potential regression when redis memory increase is applied.

sylvia: leaving now, I’ve posted step-by-step in the thread and updated the incident doc: https://incidents.redwood/P-9876. Rajesh, please escalate to SRE on-call if errors rebound above 25% of peak.

rajesh: ack taking over. I’ll monitor for next 1.5h and coordinate redis config change with infra at low traffic window.

incident-bot: P-9876 status changed to "monitoring" by rajesh.

mike: quick note for runbook improvement: add a checklist for temporary SLO overrides (who approves, auto-expire) so we can avoid leaving them open. filing follow-up RD-5433.

sylvia: +1. thanks team. closing desktop session. :wave:

rajesh: thanks all. I’ll post a short handoff summary to #oncall-ops after I confirm steady metrics.
